readerQuestion: How can I make Home Assistant turn a room light on only when someone is there and it is dark enough, without the lamp's own light breaking the routine?
directAnswer: Use a room lux reading and check darkness before turn-on. Trigger on either occupancy beginning or lux crossing below the chosen threshold, then require the pause helper on, occupancy on, lamp off and lux below the threshold. Keep optional vacancy-based shutoff independent of lux. First observe readings with the lamp off and rehearse beside one nonessential lamp; Sun is an alternative only when a night-time rule is sufficient.
originalContribution: Section 2 provides an explicitly hypothetical 75/18/140-lux calibration example and explains why 30 is only a starting threshold. Sections 3-4 provide two complete automation examples, with separate turn-on and clear-room shutoff behavior. Section 5 supplies a five-case rehearsal table covering bright entry, dark entry, darkness arriving while occupied, shutoff after clear and pause behavior, each with an expected result and a troubleshooting next step.
limitations: Documentation research and local static-site verification only; no Home Assistant instance, physical sensors or lighting hardware were tested. The YAML examples were parsed but not executed against real integrations. Reporting intervals and placement depend on the reader's exact devices. A stale numeric lux value is not detected; unknown lux blocks turn-on. Ordinary motion can clear while someone sits still. The optional off rule also affects a manually lit lamp unless paused. The for timer does not survive restart/reload and there is no catch-up routine. Re-enabling the pause helper permits future triggers, rather than immediately operating the lamp. Cover art is an AI-generated illustration, not installation evidence.

claimChecks.claim: Either of two triggers may start the routine, while occupancy and darkness must both be checked. A condition becoming true alone does not start an automation.

A numeric_state trigger reacts to crossing a threshold rather than every reading remaining below it, and the generic trigger compares raw units without conversion. The example requires a numeric lux reading.
Numeric-state conditions use exclusive bounds; exactly 30 does not satisfy below 30. Listed conditions are AND by default.
Sun calculates solar times and horizon state using the configured home location; using it as a darkness proxy does not measure the room's actual illumination.
Input boolean is a built-in toggle helper suitable for the common pause condition. In the supplied YAML it is a condition only, so switching it on does not trigger a lamp command.
The off example watches the raw occupancy state off continuously for three minutes. It does not treat an unavailable or unknown occupancy value as confirmed vacancy.
Light turn_on and turn_off are explicit actions; the example avoids toggle and avoids sending brightness/color capabilities that the reader's lamp might not expose.

Run actions bypasses triggers and top-level conditions; real input changes plus Traces are the relevant verification. Unknown or unavailable numeric states do not pass the numeric condition, and in-progress waits do not continue after restart. Current documentation locates States under Settings > Tools; older menus differ.
